segments.text: How do you feel about Gary?
It's where you all as a family spent your formative years.
Yes and that was the children's hometown.
I loved it.
Since I left though 40 some years ago Gary had made a tremendous change.
It's like a ghost town to me now because there's so many homes that are nailed up.
So many people left, Gary, because it's a steel mill town.
Gary, Chicago, Hammond, Indiana, and even parts of Chicago.
And the steel mills went down, and people lost their jobs.
And they couldn't no longer.
They had to seek work.
So they left.
And it just looks really bad.
And is that why you feel the need to go and help the community?
Yes.
But this is a town that, uh, the town, my, all my children were born there except one of my, my second son was born in East Chicago.
I was visiting my mother when I went into labor and he was born in East Chicago, Indiana, second child.
And, um, all the others were born right there in Gary.
The tribute is a two-day event.
Yes.
How important is that for you?
It's very important to me because I just feel, I feel good because people are thinking of my son that way and they want to keep his legacy alive and I like that.
I don't celebrate his birthday along with the others because I don't celebrate birthdays but everything else I take part in.
And the money that's raised, what kinds of charities will benefit?
Well, you know what I can't remember?
We just formed the charities not too long ago, and I don't remember the names of them, but...
But they're communities?
Yes, they support the community.
And it is a town that's held on to the memory of Michael?

yes yes yes i was happy about that because michael left there so many years ago he was only 11 when he left and um so um i've 10 or 11 but anyway um a lot of the people don't even know him but i know they know him by his popularity there's no one who doesn't know him i i know what i mean personally or but they're still makes me feel good
I noticed at the the tribute there will be impersonators of Michael.
Yes.
Do you enjoy watching that?
I do.
I really do.
And some people have him down so perfect, almost perfect.
Then they're dancing and doing all those moves that he does and
tell.
It brings tears to your eyes sometimes and it makes you feel good that they like what he was doing.
They're continuing it.
What was it do you think about Michael that made him so popular?
You know I
His talent was one of the things, but he was a good person, too.
He loved people.
He gave to charities.
And it's in the Guinness Book of Records that he gave more to charities than any of the stars did.
And he was down to earth.
He was very humble.
And he's very approachable.
So I think that's one of the reasons.
I mean, obviously, as his mother, you saw the seeds of that talented boy very early on.
Yeah.
What kind of child was he?
What little kind of little boy was he?
Michael, when he was young, he
He had a lot of energy, always moving around, never could sit still doing something.
I used to take him to the store when they'd try on their suits and things like that and he'd be dancing in the mirror instead of see how it could fit, he'd put it on and start dancing.
To see how it fit while he danced.
I know, and just couldn't, he had a lot of energy.
just couldn't keep still.
I noticed you said that he used to dance to the sound of the washing machine.
Yeah well that's when he was a baby.
Truly?
The rhythm of the washing machine because it was a rickety old washing machine and made those rickety and moves sounds and he started dancing to that.
Did you know then though, I mean when he was a little boy, when he was starting to show interest in music and dance, did you know then that there was something special about him?

Yes I knew it even before he was in my I knew when he was in my arms and the kids always dance around the house too and he'd see them dancing but the music comes on he was in my arms he couldn't even walk he started moving and so um I I knew it then.
But could you have ever perceived he would be the star that he became?
When he was around seven years old and the boys were singing, Jackson 5.
And I felt that if we could, somebody could see them, they would latch onto them and put them in show business.
I felt that if they were in the right place at the right time.
And, but I didn't know that it would go this far.
No, as far as it went.
And especially with Michael, because I knew he had a lot of talent, but
Then too, it took a while, you know how it was with the...
Well, I don't want to talk about that part of it, but at first back then, you know, you had, they call the thing a crossover.
Do you know what the crossover was?
No.
Well, black music was played on the black stations.
Right.
And if the song was well enough and enough whites bought it, it would cross over and they start playing it on the white stations.
And then it would go bigger, wider and wider, bigger and bigger at that time.
So, um, at that time I didn't know what to think.
but times got better and he was discovered and the group was discovered.
You have a lot of talented children.
How difficult is it when one is more successful?
How difficult is it for you as the mum?
As the mother I wish they all could have
didn't have the same success but they were all successful in a way.
Did you ever have to adjudicate?
Have to what?
Adjudicate?
Step in?
Were there ever like, how come Michael's getting all the attention?
When they were young Michael got all the attention and Marlon and Michael they they were a year apart and it was sort of
I felt bad for Marlon because he didn't get the attention that Michael got and I thought it should have been the same because by him being the same age as Michael, I imagine it bothered him.
I knew it bothered him because most people come in, I want to see little Michael, I want to see little Michael and he's standing there and my heart would just, for him.
Yeah, it's difficult, isn't it?
Because, as you said...
Yes, because both your children, you love them the same and you want them to have the same attention.
And I know it was killing him and it was hurting me too, because they would come and sit Michael on their lap and all that stuff.
and Marla just standing there looking.
Did you also understand or did you also see at that early stage what the attention might do to a young impressionable boy like Michael?
No I didn't worry about that though about because Michael was a humble person and that didn't even change him even till the day he died he was still humble.

He knew he was a big star, but you would never know that Because he treated everybody and he was always worried about his fans and he I had a lot of the securities tell me that when Michael when they got hired Michael would call him in and talk to him and he tell them always be good to my fans You know because most of the securities knock them back, you know from and he told him not to do that be nice to them
Nonetheless fame has an impact No, no matter how you try not to have an impact it does though, doesn't it?
How did it impact upon your family?
The the attention that you all got ultimately Well It's hard for me to answer that question because I'd never um Didn't have an impact on me I
When I go to the market or go to the shows or go anyplace, I'm in line like everybody else.
I've had people to come out, to come out of the theater even and say, what are you doing standing out here in the lobby?
And I told him, well, I feel that I should be in line like everybody else and I should.
And he said, no, you're family, come on in.
You know, but I didn't look at it that way.
Public, with fame comes scrutiny, public scrutiny.
Was that difficult for the family?
Well, not really.
You know, they were still singing and doing things too, so we didn't have time to even think about that.
I didn't.
By me being at home, it was a little different for me because people would see me a little different and try to treat me better, you know, but
It didn't have anything.
Perhaps you're the reason the Jacksons were so successful because you clearly are very grounded.
Is that something that comes from your upbringing?
I guess.

I've always felt that way when my children before they left home and we they were going to sign with Motown and I talked to them and I and I told them then it's just a job you're working it's like everybody else's don't let your head get too big there's no room in this house for a big head.
It would have been a lot of big heads.
Wouldn't it?
Do you think they heard you?
Do you think they understood?
Yes, they did.
I think so.
You never had to in the course of the years that follow... No, I didn't.
...to say something like, big head?
Not even to Michael?
No, no.
I think he's the most harmless one.
Do you think he felt at times awkward that he was the most successful in the family?
Uh, no, no, no.
Cause even when he was a little kid and they used to go and play for other people and he was, but still wasn't, didn't walk around like, you know, he was a big guy of a family or
But do you think he was conscious of the fact that the others weren't getting as much attention as him?
I'm sure he was.
But he's the type that would feel better, stand back and let them have their day.
Now like, I can't think of what it was, but it was Janet, I think, that went down and forgot what it was doing, but Michael wouldn't go.
he said and that was when she was just starting off and he said it's her day I don't want to go down because he would take all the attention away from her that's what he said and so he stayed home.
Because the family did come from humble beginnings yes how did money change your lives?
Well
We, we, you know, you see where we're living now, this house compared to we, they were born into a four room house, not a four bedroom, just a four room house.
That's where you began.
That's where, that's where, when I got married, we didn't have any children.
Bebe was on the way, but we didn't think we could have that many.
And it was only four little rooms in the house we bought.
We only paid $8,500 for it, brand new.
just built in and all the kids stayed there until we moved to California about 44 years ago.
So what did money do then?
What did money enable you and your family to do that you hadn't been able to do before?
It took the worries of bills and food and all of that off of our mind.
And that's the biggest thing that anybody have in their life is their food, shelter, and clothing.
We didn't have to worry about that anymore.

um and that was a big deal yes it was and we got a chance to do a lot of things that we never could do if we were dealing gary indiana we got has to see the world oh to do so many more things that we never would have had gotten the chance to do
Is money a good thing?
Pardon?
Is money a good thing?
It's a good thing in a way and it's a bad thing.
It's all in the way you use it.
And we always try to use it in a good way.
I guess it gives you choice.
Yes.
Which you don't have if you don't have money.
Right, exactly.
And it's not what you make, it's what you do with what you make.
And if you do good things with it then you reap reward.
But some people get money and they just go crazy with it.
Am I right in believing that Michael's life began to change from the moment he was severely burned doing the Pepsi commercial?
Yes.
Do you recall that day?
Yes I do, yes.
I wasn't there but I was home and I got a phone call and they told me Michael was burnt and he was on the way to the hospital and I couldn't get ready fast enough to get down there.
Did you see those bones?
At the time I didn't because they had him in there fixing him up and all but when I saw it, it was a time when he

they call the stretching of the skin and he showed me where they had put a um I don't know what it's called but it's in between your scalp and your um your head and you pump it up to keep the skin stretched so it was really bad very bad.
Did he talk to you about the effect that had upon him?
Yes, because it burned him so badly his hair wouldn't grow back in the top of his head and he didn't like that part of it.
So that's when he had to start wearing wigs.
Yes.
And I guess for a young man that's a terrible time, a terribly difficult thing to have to do.
Yes.
And for Michael Jackson, who was a performer.
They had before, before the world and he couldn't, it didn't have his hair.
It's also, as I understand, when he started to experience pain.
Yes.
Is that right?
Yes.
It was painful all the time, you know.
Did you feel your son overindulged in plastic surgery?
People might say he had overindulged in plastic surgery, but they don't know what went on before.
Michael had a disease also, and the color of his skin was changing.
The vitiligo.
I imagine it seemed like he overindulged because when he became very white and it looked different.
I think that was part of it, but
That was his choice.
And I talked to him about it.
Did you give him advice?
Oh yes, but whatever he wanted to do.
Were you worried he was having too much the facial reconstruction?
I don't know why people said he had too much.
He did change, but not that much.
He had his nose done and that really changed, because that's the center of your face and that'll change your looks.
But other than that,
I don't know what he could have done to have too much.
He had a number of relationships.
How did you feel about Maria, Lisa Marie Presley?
How do I feel about her?
Yes.
I feel perfectly fine about her.
She's a very nice person and she still comes to visit me and she was really nice and she was a good daughter-in-law.
And she cared a lot about Michael.
Yes.
Were you disappointed that that relationship didn't last?
Was I disappointed?
No, not really.
It was whatever they decided they wanted to do.
And that's what happened.
Debbie Rome?
still friends with her, still talk to her, she comes to visit, so fine.
She's a major presence now, I think, at least in Paris's life, is that right?
Yes.
And you're happy with that?
Yes, yes.
Did Michael ever talk to you about being a single dad?
sometimes he would.
Because that was a big decision wasn't it to have children and without a partner?
Well he always wanted to be a dad father and when he and Debbie divorced he kept the children and so um and he's he was a wonderful dad.
Did you find it difficult?
Not really

Grace used to tell me how he would cook for them and they would think it was the best food in the world just because he did it and Paris still talks about it, you know, but But he loved it and and the children obviously You don't believe there were any worse off without having a mother in their lives When

not really because he always had a um nanny there and he was always there too with them and um i don't think they they really missed a mother because they never had it so never knew you know because when she when she when they divorced they were still babies so and they were cared for just as well as if a mother was there
Did you worry at all that when they made public appearances they were wearing masks?
Well I didn't like that part of it that's why when Michael passed I never put them on him.
But Michael did it for a reason.
He said that when the children would ever go out with their friends or Michael's friends like
Kathy Hilton Was a good friend of the Michaels and my children because they all went to school together That's Paris Hilton's mother.
That's how Paris got her name.
Oh, she's named after Paris Hilton.
Who?
Sorry, Paris.
No Paris Hilton got her name because when the kids were young and they were all in school Paris Kathy Hilton and Michael and Latoya they were all friends and I
We went on a trip to Chicago and the boys were singing there and there was a
a security guard.
He was a man, but his name was Paris.
And they fell in love with the name.
So when they came back to school, they told Paris Hilton, we ever have a girl, we're going to all name our girl Paris.
But she had the girl first.
So she did.
And then it fit her because Paris Hilton, like the Hilton Hotel.
Correct.
And LaToya had a little puppy and she named it Paris.
And so when Michael had his first daughter, he named her Paris.
So that's how the name came about.
Well what was the question I was supposed to be asking?
It was about how you thought about them having masks and wearing disguises.
Oh like yes and I was going to use Paris' Cathy Hilton because she was always visiting Michael and she would take the kids to the park and everything.
So Michael said if I disguise them when I'm with them because they'll know they're Michael's children if I didn't.
So when they're out there with
Kathy or any of the other people They can have fun.
They wouldn't know who children they were Because that's when they're gonna see their faces and when they're back with Michael he covers it again And I don't know that sounds good.
But you know, the kids didn't have a problem with it Do they ever talk about that now?
Paris does and what does she likes it?
She talked about that's why daddy did it, you know
So they understood.
Yes, they did.
Do you recall the very public episode when Michael held one of the children over a balcony?
You mean blanket?
Oh, yeah, I do.
I recall that but don't ask me what I felt or what I said or whatever.
I was wondering, I imagine Michael was exuberant, he was happy, and perhaps not realising how that would be interpreted.
No, yeah, I wasn't thinking.
Did you talk to him about that?
No, I just told him how to invite him to do it, you know, and that was it.
Shouldn't have done that.
These are some difficult questions so I'll leave it up to you how you deal with them but Michael obviously suffered in terms of his reputation and allegations of child molestation.
How did that impact the family?
It was hard on me
I knew all the time Michael didn't do it.
You had no doubt?
I had no doubt.
I knew he didn't do it.
Did you ever ask him?
I didn't have to.
We talked about it all the time.
We talked about things.
Both families lied.
Do you wish that Michael had not paid?
Wish he hadn't I got and I told him As a mother that makes you angry doesn't it?
Yes, it does make me angry because he looked guilty When he do that, but what they did they left that case open I think Janice was it ten years ten years left it open ten years and
And they said, if anybody, Michael had touched any kid or anything like that come, it's open for 10 years.
Nobody came.
And since, I don't know if you've read it, but since Michael died, Geordie Chandler came and said, Michael didn't touch me.
He didn't do anything to me.
I wish I could have.
Did you read that?
I was going to ask you about that.
I did read that and I was, he never came to you or anybody?
He wanted to.
And during that 2005 case, he had told a friend of ours that was a journalist.
And he told him, he said, I want to go to Michael.
Where is he?
I want to find him.
Because I'm going out in general to tell the public about, you know, he was going to do that.
But he never did.

They told me, and then the insurance company, they told him, not the insurance company, but somebody told him not to do it because if he had gone out and did it, they would make them pay that money back to the insurance company.
And he never, so during that 2005 trial, he left the country, because he didn't want to come and be on stage.
I mean on Stan's stand.
Because he would have to tell the truth.
And so his father was there in New York.
But when he did announce, finally after Michael died, his father committed suicide.
And I wondered about that.
Why would he kill himself?
The reason I was going to ask you about whether Jordan Chandler had recounted or recanted his allegations was because it's also been refuted that he's said that.
So no one in the family's actually had direct conversation with Jordan Chandler.

after that Jordan Chandler hasn't come to you or any member of the family to say those allegations were untrue you've just heard that reported I heard that reported but he told Michael that and Michael said well why don't you tell it that was when he was still a kid and you know he divorced himself from his parents back then because they did that and made him do that to him
What kind of weight did this all carry on Michael?
Did it dictate everything he did in life from that point on?
What do you mean by dictate?
Well, it affected all his decision making from that point on.
These allegations hurt him so much.
Did you find that he changed, Michael changed, once he was having to fight these allegations?
Well, you know, at first he
I don't see why he made a change because he was still, he still had friends, he still had children all over.
And they were still lying in the papers and they put, they saw Michael's cousins was with them in the swimming pool.
Helicopter floor took pictures.
And the first thing I saw in the papers was Michael Jackson and these little boys.
And their grandmother saw it.
And she was in the store.
And then she heard the clerks talking about it.
She got really upset.
And she said, those are my grandchildren.
And those are Michael's cousins.
And we were over there visiting.
And he was in the pool with the kids.
These are very painful allegations, aren't they, for a mother to hear?
Yes, it is, because I know any little thing that people trying to, what it is, it's the news.
That's what keeps mess going.
And at one time I thought the world is nothing but a cesspool.
They just want to hear garbage.
My son-in-law,
James Abarge that was married to Janet, he came to me and said that they came to him and they wanted him to talk about the family.
And he said, and he started talking and all this good stuff and they said, we don't want that.
And they said, do you know anything bad that they did?
He said, no.
And you know what they told him?
Make something up.
So if we went to sue the paper,
we'd have to sue him because he said it.
That's all it was.
And that's all people do.
They don't want to hear good stuff.
They just want to hear garbage.
How do you then deal with this in terms of Michael's children?
Do they know about these allegations?
Well, they might know now.
I don't know.
But during that time, they didn't know.
They haven't asked you about them?
No.
Do you fear that day?
Do you dread that day?
That they will ask me.
I'll just tell them how I feel.
And I'm sure they might feel the same way.
I'm sure they do.
Because they know their father.
They know better.
It's difficult, isn't it?
Because that's probably one of the things they will have to confront is an avalanche of stories about their dad.
How do you prepare them for that?
Just talk to them and tell them the truth, that's all.
You can't immune them though, can you, from what others say to them?
Pardon?
You can't immune them from what others say to them?
No, no I can't.
Have they had any
tough times in terms of what other people have said at school or out socially?
I don't know if they have they haven't told me but they might have.
On the day Michael died where were you?
I came home
And their father called me and he said, can't you have to come down to the hospital?
I went down and nobody would say anything.
Everybody was waiting for somebody else to tell me.
And I saw Dr. Murray Pacing, but I didn't know who he was.
And I said, well, where's Michael?
I want to go to his room.
I want to go and visit him.
Nobody said anything.
And then finally in about 10 or 15 minutes later, they took me to a room and nobody still didn't say anything.
So finally I said, well, did he make it?
And I was screaming like, did he make it?
And Frank finally said slowly, no, he didn't make it.
I don't know what happened after that.
I guess I must have blacked out or screamed or something.
But that's what happened.
I don't know how mother deals with that.
That was the worst day of my life.
Never had that feeling before.
And I never want to feel like that again.
But had you never feed this day would come there were never thought this day would come Now how has it changed your life Well
I have three children, three more children to raise, animals again, things like that.
At your wonderful age, do you feel okay to be a mother again?
Yes, yes.
Today it's a little more difficult than it was in the day I raised my kids because a little more harder because the world changed a lot.
But it's not hard, but it's fine.
What's different these days than it was back then?

Well then back in our day it was so They had too much out there that children can get a hold of and they talk about too much in the movies even when When I was a kid In the in the movies they slept in twin beds the pop father and the mother fully clothed
No, today you go to the movies and they're naked or they're having sex and all this stuff.
It's hard to, you know, in some of the movies they've got everything.
So much killing, so much doing all this.
So you, it's really, it's still tough.
How do you, yeah, how do you discipline that?
How do you, what do you do?
Just talk to the children.
And is that the secret?
Communication?
Yes.
And what do they say to you?
They obviously view you as the rock in their life.
Well, they talk about things, but they never get too deep in any subject, like the killing and the shooting and all of that stuff or into sex or anything like that.
Do they talk about their dad's death?
No.
Well, no.
Have they ever?
Is death?
Have they ever discussed their dad's death?
No.
Would you like them to?
I think that's what it might not be.
Not really.
Not really.
The only thing they always bring their father up when they talk to one another and sometimes they'd say dad did it this way or you know dad wouldn't like that or something like that.
I hear that quite often but other things like that I don't.
What wouldn't dad like?
What sort of things wouldn't dad like?
Well when the children are being naughty or
They felt like that.
But when Michael died and Paris was screaming and crying and saying, I want to go with you, Daddy.
I don't want to live without you.
And all these things.
I was feeling so bad for her.
Paris clearly has suffered very badly.
She did.
She had to have his pictures everywhere in her room.
Every picture that was hanging on the wall had to be Michael.
And then finally she went to a life coach and they told her, take the pictures down.
Because I guess she was suffering and we didn't know it.
And she did.
It is reported that she tried to commit suicide.
Is that true?
Then she might have.
She didn't know how maybe, I don't know.
But yes it is.
And
So I don't know what made her do something like that.
Have you talked to her about it?
Not really, because since she did that
she had therapists and all of that that's been talking with her about all that kind of stuff.
Do you want to talk to her about it?
I will but not right now when whenever she's finished with all her other therapies then I'll talk to her.
Did they get to say goodbye to their dad?
Pardon?
Did they get to say goodbye to their dad?
No, I don't think so.
Because they went back in that morgue where Michael was about 10 times when I was in that room.
I couldn't go.
And so when Latoya came she kept going back there too.
I said what are you all doing back there?
She said the children are hugging Michael and kissing him and you know he was dead but they were still doing that.
You didn't want to see Michael?
Not that way, no.
I wanted to remember him when he was smiling and he was alive.
And you have no regrets about that?
No I don't.
No, I talked.
Clearly Michael's passing has caused some stresses in the family from time to time.
I hadn't thought about that until that happened but no, not, you know.
You know what, since Michael's passing have caused problems
in a lot of ways.
But you know what, I shouldn't even say this because it has to do with court.
No, I'm not going to talk about court.
I'm not talking about court.
I'm just saying people are so greedy and people are stealing and people are doing everything, taking things from up from under you that things that rightfully should be yours.
And they're, you know, all that happens when people die, especially if a person, um, they think they got a lot of money and they got things that they want and things like that.
Everything's happening.
So,
It's a terrible position to be in, isn't it?
Because I think of all the people that Michael knew and loved, it's you he trusted most.
He always told me I was the only one he trusted.
That's because he lost trust.
His problem was he trusts too much.
And he went, I should say, from a baby.
He grew up in show business.
He didn't have time to learn about people.
He didn't know how dirty people was.
And my helper would always tell him, Michael, watch your stuff.
Be careful with these people.
Watch your stuff.
You know, he'd always say, know where your money's going.
And he always would tell him, he said, Joe, I trust my people.
I have good people.
He thought he had.
But see, they took advantage of him.
He's not the first artist performer to have that situation occur.
No, no, no.
A lot of people do.
Because the people that are taking care of your things are just dirty people.
And they just... Did Michael grow up, do you think?
Did he grow up?
In so many ways he grew up.
In so many ways,
I shouldn't say he didn't.
in a way, what do you mean when you say, did he grow up?
I mean it kindly.
I know, but what do you mean?

He seemed, for example, you know, he had the pet chimp, the pet monkey bubbles, and he had, you know, he wanted childlike things around him, it seems, like, you know, fun rides, and it was like that childhood he was clinging to.
Even though he was now a man, you know, in his 40s and 50s.
Well, you know, it's been reported that way.
And Michael built Neverland on his ranch.
And he had a petting zoo and he had elephants and camels and monkeys and chimps and everything like that.
And it wasn't just for him.
He built it for other children that not successful.
All the time, the classrooms of children would come.
And so we talked about it a lot.
